blocks.title: Loan and interest
blocks.text: A loan is borrowed money that must be paid back with interest. Interest is the cost of borrowing, usually a percentage of the loan amount.
A Multan tea shop borrows Rs 100,000 at 10% a year: total repayment = 100,000 + 10% x 100,000 = Rs 110,000 after one year.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: what is repaid on Rs 50,000 for one year at 8%, and how does the rate affect the total?
blocks.explanation: Interest = 8% x 50,000 = Rs 4,000, so the total is Rs 54,000. A higher rate raises the interest in proportion; at 10% it would be Rs 55,000.

blocks.prompt: Explain the significance of financial management and how budgeting and cash flow affect operations (long question 6).
blocks.explanation: Financial management keeps a business alive: it tracks revenue and costs to protect profit, plans spending through budgets, saves for equipment and emergencies, and decides when borrowing is worth the interest. A budget shows where money should go and warns of overspending. Cash flow, the timing of money coming in and going out, matters because even a profitable business fails if it cannot pay rent and salaries on time; planning cash flow avoids such gaps. Cash flow is not explained in the chapter; this part is general knowledge.
